newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Both London and New York remained quiet ahead of the New Year Holidays. White sugar prices in London closed unchanged to higher with spot March adding $0.40 to close at $309.20. May added $0.10 to close at $308.50. In New York raw sugar futures closed in an abbreviated session barely higher but gains were enough to lift the most-active March contract through key psychological resistance at 11.00 cents/lb. The increase over the past few days was due mainly to fund-buying. Given current bearish fundamentals the market looks overbought.

THAILAND - According to industry sources sugar exports in 1996/97 (November/October) could reach 4.8 million tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 4.6 million tonnes. Exports in 1994/95 reached 3.8 million tonnes. Production in 1996/97 is estimated at 6.28 million tonnes, tel quel, while domestic consumption is forecast at 1.7 million tonnes. However, the Thai industry expects lower prices than last year, given forecasts of another world surplus in 1996/97.

PAKISTAN - Sugar production for fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) fell 42.87 per cent to 388,272 tonnes by December 15 compared to 679,635 tonnes the year-ago period, the Pakistan Sugar Mills Association said. The fall is due to the late start of the campaign and large scale diversion of cane to producers of alternative sweeteners. However, in spite of the lower production so far the industry expects the total in 1996/97 to rise to 2.65 million tonnes, tel quel, up from 2.47 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 3.0 million tonnes in 1994/95.

BRAZIL - Sugar exports in November 1996 amounted to 777,238 tonnes, raw value, slightly up on last year's 766,881 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (May/November) up to 4.111 million tonnes, down from 4.637 million tonnes exported in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 hit the record high of 5.922 million tonnes compared to 4.352 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in May/November 1996 were Nigeria with 382,940 tonnes whites against 258,296 tonnes, Russia with 267,449 tonnes compared to 486,898 tonnes, Algeria with 233,950 tonnes against 251,949 tonnes and Egypt with 273,718 tonnes, down from 488,757 tonnes. The largest destination for Brazilian raw sugar were the USA with 123,012 tonnes compared to 26,855 tonnes.

SINGAPORE - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 27,405 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 28,157 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of calendar year 1996 (January/September) up to 225,903 tonnes against 203,389 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 271,334 tonnes against 285,420 tonnes in 1994 and 262,186 tonnes in 1993. Major countries of origin in January/September 1996 were Thailand with 80,000 tonnes raws, up from last year's 8,000 tonnes, Australia with 40,001 tonnes compared to 134,013 tonnes and Malaysia with 51,893 tonnes whites, up from last year's 35,742 tonnes. Sugar exports in January/September 1996 reached 8,111 tonnes, down from last year's 15,593 tonnes. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 22,136 tonnes against 23,391 tonnes in 1994. The major country of destination in January/September 1996 was Brunei with 1,553 tonnes whites against 1,273 tonnes.
